original_question: How can one describe all transcendental meromorphic solutions of the difference equation f(z + c1)^2 + f(z + c2)^2 = f(z)^2, where c1 and c2 are fixed distinct nonzero constants?
target_in_paper: Section 1: the Proposition 1.2 reformulation of Conjecture 1.1, resolved in Theorem 1.3, concerning finite-order transcendental meromorphic solutions of the quadratic three-term shift equation closest to f(z+c1)^2+f(z+c2)^2=f(z)^2.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right unknown object class at a high level (transcendental meromorphic functions) and the right core quadratic shift equation with two fixed distinct nonzero shifts c1 and c2. It also asks for a classification rather than a mere existence statement, which is aligned with the paper’s intent in the nearby Conjecture 1.1/Proposition 1.2/Theorem 1.3 chain.
missing_details: The paper’s nearby official formulation is about finite-order transcendental meromorphic solutions, not arbitrary transcendental meromorphic growth.
The ambient domain should be stated explicitly: f is meromorphic on the complex plane C and the equation is required to hold for all z in C.
The draft does not say that c1,c2 are complex constants in C\{0} with c1 != c2.
The paper’s exact nearby formulation is tied to an equivalent reformulation in Proposition 1.2; that equivalence should be reflected if one wants the question to be paper-faithful.
The intended description is not just verbal; it is in terms of an explicit Riccati-type/parametric representation for the shift quotients.

The phrase “describe all solutions” should be sharpened to “classify all finite-order transcendental meromorphic solutions” and, if using the equivalent formulation, include the compatibility relations for the auxiliary meromorphic generator.
The quantifier 'for all z in C' is implicit in your draft but should be written explicitly.
The paper-faithful version should stay narrowly on this exact quadratic homogeneous shift equation and not broaden to neighboring Fermat-type equations.
refined_question: Let c1,c2 be fixed complex constants with c1,c2 \in C\setminus\{0\} and c1 \neq c2. Classify all finite-order transcendental meromorphic functions f on C such that, for every z \in C, one has f(z+c1)^2+f(z+c2)^2=f(z)^2; equivalently, determine the exact Riccati-type representation of all such solutions that the paper obtains in its Proposition 1.2/Theorem 1.3 formulation.
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently (as reformulated in Proposition 1.2), determine all finite-order transcendental meromorphic functions f for which there exists a meromorphic auxiliary function \omega on C satisfying, for all z \in C, f(z+c1)=(2\omega(z)/(1+\omega(z)^2))f(z) and f(z+c2)=((1-\omega(z)^2)/(1+\omega(z)^2))f(z); this parametrization is exactly the paper’s explicit reformulation of f(z+c1)^2+f(z+c2)^2=f(z)^2.
justification: The closest official paper statement to your draft is not a broader open-ended question about arbitrary meromorphic solutions, but the Conjecture 1.1 -> Proposition 1.2 -> Theorem 1.3 package in Section 1. Your draft matches the Proposition 1.2/Theorem 1.3 side of that package because it already uses the homogeneous quadratic shift equation with the two distinct nonzero shifts. What it misses, relative to the paper, is the finite-order restriction, the explicit quantification over z in C, and the fact that the classification is expressed through a Riccati-type auxiliary parametrization rather than by an informal description. So the refined version keeps your exact equation, adds only the paper-critical restrictions and quantifiers, and points to the equivalent Riccati-type formulation because that is the paper’s own sharpening of the problem.
